column1: # Compile-time scaling budgets (R-0550, ROADMAP Phase 1 exit 2o): the record
#   shape   NAME SIZES MODES        a generated shape, its sizes and the compiles it is timed by
#   exclude SHAPE STAGES REASON     stages (a comma list, or *) not judged, with the filed defect
#                                   or the reason they are not measured
#   budget  SHAPE SIZE STAGE MS     written by `check_compile_scaling.sh --measure` on the CI host
#   hbbudget SHAPE SIZE STAGE COUNT allocation heartbeats a stage may make (exact; bug 294)
#   instr   SHAPE SIZE MODE COUNT   retired user instructions a run may take (perf; bug 294)
#   rate    SHAPE SIZE MODE MS      that run's ms per 10^9 instructions at --measure: the host
#                                   speed the wall budgets are normalized to (bug 294)
#   a `measured:` stamp naming shapes covers exactly those shapes' budgets (each shape is named
#   by at most one stamp); the stamp naming none covers every other shape
# Budgets are re-measured (and the `measured:` line restamped) only on the CI host class: a change
# that legitimately moves a stage re-measures, a change that breaks one fixes the compiler.
# exp, hb_exp: sizes are a factor of ten apart, and a quadratic stage grows x100. A linear stage's
# allocations (heartbeats) grow exactly x10, so hb_exp 1.2 (x15.8) is tight. Its time grows more
# (caches, the allocator, memory bandwidth shared with other jobs): up to x35 on the loaded CI host
# and x52 with eight gates running at once on the dev host, fastest of three attempts; exp 1.8
# (x63) sits above that, and judges only a run perf did not count on a host that counts. A mixed
# stage whose quadratic part is still small at these sizes can pass the time bound and is held by its
# Bug 294: wall budgets measured on a quiet host failed unchanged work on the loaded CI host (one
# binary's monomorphize stage at 10^5 assignments took 261 - 575 ms at load 24 against a 412 ms
# budget, the same 13.615 G instructions each time). hbbudget and instr hold a run's work exactly
# (hb_budget_factor and instr_budget_factor above the --measure counts: a change that legitimately
# adds work re-measures). instr_exp 1.06 (x11.5 for x10) bounds a counted run's instruction growth
# above its one-line baseline: a linear compile grows x10.0 - x10.3 there and a quadratic part 1.6 %
# of the run at 10^4 exceeds it; such a run's stages are not judged for wall growth (exp, below), whose
# ratio measures the caches as much as the work (compile_scaling.py, GROWTH). A wall budget is
# judged on the stage's time divided by how much slower than `rate` its run went per instruction,
# at most norm_cap: so load cannot fail unchanged work up to norm_cap, added work still shows in
# instr, and only a change that makes the same instructions slower is excused, up to norm_cap.
# --measure scales each run to the session's quietest rate and keeps the fastest; that removes the
# variation between runs, not load lasting the whole session, so it refuses a host whose load average
# is above measure_max_load (32 threads: 8 is a quarter busy) and stamps the load it ran at.
# Bug 315: where perf cannot count instructions:u (the dev host), wall growth and wall budgets are
# NOT JUDGED (the gate exits 77, which the CI-gates runner records as deferred to CI, never as a pass);
# only a stage over uncounted_fail_factor x its budget (40 x the CI host's quiet median, at least 2 s)
# still fails there, a level no load reaches (load slowed stages x2 - x3 in bugs 294 and 315). CI must
# count: an uncounted CI runner fails the gate.
# Declaration and nesting shapes run at 10^4 and 10^5 with their whole compiles since bugs 280,
# 286, 288 - 293 (R-0550 follow-up); functions and call-chain are compiled natively only by the
# other shapes (clang alone takes 80 - 130 s on 10^5 functions). lets-if and lets-match run at
# (their native compile at 10^5 takes 30 - 40 s); lets-while at 2000 and 20000, front end only (bug 270).

# measured: commit a37ec8ee5fc44e3f16a4e15fda881f05ccef40f5 on concrete-ci-2, AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D 16-Core Processor, 32 threads, 2026-10-27, 3 runs (fastest run, each scaled to the quietest instruction rate of the session; load average 1.3 at the end), budget = max(4 x t, t + 200ms)

column4: bug 270 (open): Lower gives every loop a header phi for every binding in scope, so this shape's lower stage is quadratic (4.9, 18.7 and 51.7 s at 1000, 2000 and 4000 at b5040d53); --emit-trace-json runs Lower, so monomorphize is not timed apart from it, and the front end is judged through --emit-core
